Selecting a dot then clicking an empty cell does NOTHING. So the move I saw at idx116 was NOT a simple "select + click empty".
Let me reconsider idx116. Before: dots at (1,1),(1,2),(1,4),(1,5) [cols 13,19,31,43]. I selected (1,1) [col 14≈13] at idx115. Then clicked (1,3) [col 26≈25] at idx116. After: dots at (1,3),(1,4),(1,5) [cols 25,31,43].
So the dot at (1,1) [col 13] and (1,2) [col 19] became (1,3) [col 25].
Wait, maybe the click at (16,14) was NOT on a dot. Col 14 is in cell (1,1) [cols 13-16], which had a dot. So it was on a dot.
And the click at (16,26) was on cell (1,3) [cols 25-28], which was empty.
Result: 2 dots (1,1),(1,2) became 1 dot at (1,3).
This is a MERGE of two adjacent dots (1,1) and (1,2) into (1,3)?? That's not adjacent-merge.
OR: the selected dot (1,1) merged with the dot at (1,2) (its neighbor), and the result is placed at the CLICKED cell (1,3).
So the rule might be: select dot A, click cell C. If A has an adjacent dot B, then A and B merge into C?
That's bizarre.
Alternatively, maybe I'm misreading the cells. Let me recompute: col 13 → (13-7)//6 = 1 → cell (1,1). col 19 → (19-7)//6 = 2 → cell (1,2). col 25 → (25-7)//6 = 3 → cell (1,3). Yes.
So (1,1)+(1,2) → (1,3).
Hmm, what if the merge is: select dot, click a cell, and ALL dots to the LEFT of the clicked cell (up to the selected one) merge into the clicked cell?
This is too speculative.
Let me try a DIFFERENT clean experiment: select a dot, then click ANOTHER DOT (not empty). See if they merge.

Select (1,3) [col 26], click (1,4) [col 32, a dot]. See if they merge.

sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def ndots(fr):
    a=fr.ascii.split('\n'); pts=set()
    for r in range(9,60):
        for c2 in range(7,60):
            if a[r][c2]=='N': pts.add((r,c2))
    seen=set(); out=[]
    for p in pts:
        if p in seen: continue
        st=[p]; comp=[]
        while st:
            q=st.pop()
            if q in seen or q not in pts: continue
            seen.add(q); comp.append(q); r,cc=q
            for dr,dc in((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                if (r+dr,cc+dc) in pts: st.append((r+dr,cc+dc))
        out.append((min(x[0] for x in comp),min(x[1] for x in comp)))
    return sorted(out)
# select dot (1,3) col26, click dot (1,4) col32
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':16,'col':26}])
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':16,'col':32}])
print("dot+dot merge:", ndots(current_frame))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
